svg.title: Cofactor roles and attachment
svg.desc: B vitamins supply chemical carriers. NAD cycles as a cosubstrate while FAD in succinate dehydrogenase stays bound. PDH uses TPP, lipoamide, CoA, FAD and NAD for linked decarboxylation, acyl transfer and redox steps.
svg.text: Cofactors: role and attachment are separate
1 Match the carrier to the chemical job
B₃ → NAD(P): redox • B₂ → FAD/FMN: redox
B₅ → CoA: acyl groups • B₇ → biotin: carboxyl groups
B₉ → THF: one-carbon units • B₆ → PLP: amino-acid chemistry
2 Coenzyme and cosubstrate can both apply
NAD⁺ enters a reaction → NADH leaves → NAD⁺ regenerated
FAD in succinate dehydrogenase stays enzyme-bound.
Prosthetic groups may be covalently OR tightly noncovalently bound.
E2 + lipoamide + CoA: transfer the acetyl group
E3 + FAD + NAD⁺: restore oxidized lipoamide
Overall products include acetyl-CoA, CO₂ and NADH.
